title: Is community support for this engine dead?

posts.author: deathsia
posts.body:
I ask because I CAN'T FIND ANYTHING when i look for it.
I want a tall character generator, NOPE UNLESS I'VE GOT 100 BUCKS!
I want to add a custom gauge to my game that lets me edit values of how it fills and/or is depleted, NOPE! NOT UNLESS I FORK OVER 8-10 BUCKS!
I post a thread offering to pay people to make me a plugin, IT HAS BEEN ALMOST 6 MONTHS AND NOT A SINGLE REPLY.
And don't even point me to that ghost forum known as the plugin request section. EVERYONE knows that the only people who go there are people desperate for a plugin for their project and the odds of a plugin maker of any actual skill, going to that forum section and offering to make any of the requested plugins is about as likely as the sun exploding today.
Same goes for the resource request section of the forums. :/
My point is, either this community has devolved into a greedy cash driven community, or people have overall abandoned the engine.
And no, do not point me to
The MZ Plugin List
as most plugins listed there either don't do what I want, cost too much, or are so outdated its not even close to funny.
Not to mention EVEN IF I DO, the odds of them being compatible with one another is about as likely as the earth ending tomorrow.
Yanfly used to be my go-to plugin creditor for years...and then he went pay-to-use and I have no idea why, greed? Financial hardship? No idea.
I'm not saying plugins are non-existent, just that finding one that does specially what I need is like finding a needle in a haystack and most that actually do what i need cost money.  I'm not saying plugin devs don't deserve to be paid for their work but this community literally RUNS on the generosity and creativity of plugin devs making free to use plugins.
And lord help if me if i want to go commercial, half those "free" plugins require me to pay out in order to use them to make a profit!

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body: The userbase became smaller and the average age of users went up. Less users = less "kind hearted" people to do free work, older users = less willing to work for free. Pretty soon I'll start sending bills to all the people I reply here too. Also the whole world culture shifted to less generous one. But yeah, if you're not willing to pay 8$ for a plugin, I guess most devs don't think you'd pay enough to take up any offers.

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
What in creation are you talking about? The Resource Requests forum is alive and well.
But also--check your attitude, dude. Making demands is one of the fastest ways to make the generous folks who might take a request stroll right on by. If you haven't read the
How To Request Stuff The Better Way
,
How To Make A Resource Reques
t, and
Why Does No One Want To Help Me With My Game
threads, I recommend them.
Mobile typing, posted this before I was done, more to come.
This used to be a hobbyist-dominated field--people made things for fun, not profit, and so loads of things--both games and resources--were available for free. But as it became easier to publish a game or an asset for a price, people began realizing they could be paid for their work. "Hobby" became "side hustle," especially for asset creators. And reasonably so--it's skilled labor.
There are lots of things still generously provided by the community. You just have to spend your time searching, and be kind when you ask for help. It goes a long way.

posts.author: Miggmaru

requiring money for a normally free product to be used to make money is a very normal and standard thing, even outside of plugins. Most commission artists that have a TOS either don't allow commercial use of their paid work or have a different price and terms of service for it because they should be properly compensated for what the commissioner benefiting from them. Why would anyone just let you sell their free work?? What.
It's hilarious you mention yanfly. I feel so bad for them; part of the reason they went to a paid model is because people kept disrespecting the sheer metric ton of work they put in, and then people KEPT TRYING TO USE THEIR WORK WITHOUT PERMISSION even after that. And you literally called the community itself cash hungry and greedy. Wym you didn't call anyone greedy for wanting to be paid?
And like. I get the frustration of not being able to learn new skills easily. My developmental disorder makes it so I'm always going to learn slower and have a harder time obtaining skills than the average person. I bawl my eyes out about it about every month! But that doesn't mean I'm entitled to creative services I in no way need to live, and honestly it makes me respect people for what they can accomplish even more. The audacity in every reply you post...

how

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Let's try to reduce the character bashing and look at some facts for why the experiences of the OP went wrong.
More specifically the classified request already linked above:
https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/index.php?threads/requesting-a-coder-to-create-a-custom-combat-engine-paid.175568/
Your biggest problem with that request was that you didn't post a budget at all.
And I'm not talking about the rules that require setting a budget (although it was bad that the mod who approved it overlooked that in your walls of text).
No, the problem is that the big description of the work was followed by a rather short description of you requiring the people who answer to be willing to negotiate or to accept a payment plan if their price is too high, without mentioning what is "too high" for you.
That left everyone one interested with an image of someone who thought he could get such a massive request on the cheap, and no one bothered to even check what you truly would have paid.
If you had written something like "If the price is higher than I expect, I need to pay in monthly instalments of $200 or less", then I suspect you would have gotten answers because that would have shown that you know that such a plugin commission could easily go into multiple hundreds of dollars.

posts.author: Tai_MT
posts.body:
deathsia said:
The best skillset I could provide would be storywriting and don't say "anyone can do it."
Click to expand...
As a story writer... I highly doubt you have a "story wsriting" skillset in the slightest.  You aren't even well versed enough in real psychology of people to be able to write a believable and coherent character, just based upon your replies and constant "doubling down" as well as "hostility".
deathsia said:
because As someone whose been writing for 15+yrs and has seen many fanfics and stories, anyone can throw a piece of garbage 20k words together and call it a "story" but it takes a talented writer to make something people enjoy reading.
Click to expand...
A talented writer rarely believes they are, themselves, talented in the craft.
Why?  They're constantly learning.  Constantly fixing their old mistakes.
"The artists harshest critic of their work, is themselves".  This is more true than you know.  Any truly talented artist I've seen (regardless of the craft they have chosen) usually feels most of their work is "passable" or "decent" or "could be a lot better".  Rarely does a very talented artist reach the pinnacle of where they desire to be, which is the place they would measure as "being great at the craft".
But, you do get a lot of posers who will self-proclaim their greatness.
How's that quote go?  "You don't have to tell people you're great.  They can see you are.".
Anyhow, now that I'm done being personally and professionally antagonized by your comments on "being a writer", I'll comment on your request (which I haven't seen before I've made this post.  Yes, I stopped what I was writing to you, to read it in full, to give you feedback.  Something you should be comfortable having and have the ability to parse maturely, if you ARE, in fact, A STORY WRITER OF 15 YEARS).
1.  It sounds like you're requesting essentially an entirely new combat engine or a total conversion.  I don't code, but the depth of your request sounds like literal months of work.
2.  Your description of your needs is less "These are the things I need the plugin to do" and more "This is an in depth explanation of how my game actually functions".
Just as an example, do we really NEED to know what your states are?  I wouldn't think so.  You're requesting control over current ATB bars as well as a second bar, and the ability to tie their "filling" to specific actions enemies take, actors take, or just based on amount of game ticks going by.
I would have probably summarized your first 10 paragraphs like this:
"Hey, I need to request a plugin where there's a second ATB gauge on screen, and I have access to determine how fast those bars fill through enemy hits, player actions, and probably also states.  As an example, if my player throws a fireball and it hits the enemy, their first gauge fills slower.  Meanwhile, if the enemy depletes one of the player's bars, I can have it trigger a state/action if I want.  I would also like control over the bars enough that if one fills, I can fill a second one, or I can have actions also activate when bars are full."
The next few paragraphs sound like an entirely new plugin altogether in which you have a menu interface and some sort of mini-game programmed on top of it (it sounds like you want someone to literally program the mini-game for you, the way you've phrased it all in here).  I'm not even entirely sure how you'd make these next paragraphs into a coherent plugin.  Usually you would just request "I need this feature, and need it to do X" so that you can get a lot of versatility out of it, rather than something highly specific (especially with the way you state you want your combat system to work, you'd DEFINITELY be needing a lot of versatility rather than something hyper specific, so you can tweak it as needed, and as you go to balance your game).
If I'm a plugin creator, I've already checked out of your post by this point, before even hitting your "split" of where you actually specify what it is you're looking for.
3.  You are too specific in what you want, I think.  You ask for "assets to be created", but what if those assets clash with what you want?  Or it doesn't fit the window style?  You don't even specify that you'd like to be able to "customize" what the bars look like (color, thickness, whatever) on your end.  Just a blanket "I need any ol' bars" with the unspoken part of "If I don't like what you decided on, I'll need to ask you to do more work for me, to fix them to what I like.  Possibly even months later, if my project has changed".
This request sounds reallllllyyyyyyy high maintenance and annoying with some "obvious business red flags".
4.  The screenshots are a good touch.  I wish we had more "mock ups" of what you might be looking for.  But, the screenshots at least detail what you're hoping to use in the notes and how those might be set up.
5.
deathsia said:
I would kindly ask that the plugin developer be patent with me as I often have trouble clearly conveying my intentions and have a tendency to overcomplicate things and can be slow to understand why the "simple method" is more efficient until thoroughly explained to me. So revisions may be needed in those cases. I will also need to ensure compatibility with plugins i am currently using so once someone accepts my offer i will speak with them regarding this.
Click to expand...
This.
If the plugin writer hadn't checked out of your post by this point, this is going to be "the final nail in the coffin".
You are literally saying, "I will probably tie up all your time and bandwidth because I don't know exactly what I want and can't convey it to you".
This is before we even get into the problems these personality traits have to BEING A WRITER.
This paragraph you posted here is a bright neon sign saying "stay away.  Only woe exists beyond this point".
To put it into perspective:
I occasionally (not often, as I am very controlling over my own work) have people ask me to do writing for them.  Not necessarily for games here (okay, basically never here
My reputation preceeds me as well as my insanely massive walls of text), but for other projects.  I learned pretty early on that when someone is making stipulations like this...  They are wasting my time.
What they say they are asking for is "someone to work with them", but it's basically always, "someone to imagine exactly what's in my head, and then create it for me, exactly as I envisioned it".  Nobody can do that.  It's a waste of time to cater to anyone who insinuates that's what they're trying to do.
These types of people are one of the reasons I started using contracts.  They are also the reason I started stipulating "If I create it, and you decide not to use it, or to part ways to me, it still belongs to me, and you can no longer use it".  Because, I'll be Beaver Dammed if I put forth effort into someone else's pet project and get nothing out of it as the person asking for the help gradually loses interest and passion and/or decides I'm "not good enough" to reach into their head to pull forth what they imagine, whole cloth, into the world like I'm a freakin' psychic.
My contracts are "onerous" because of people who have this attitude that you've posted in this paragraph.  What I create is MINE until you RELEASE and I RESERVE THE RIGHT TO REVOKE USAGE AT ANY POINT UNTIL THEN.  That's usually how I roll, because of people who make these sorts of paragraphs or have these sorts of attitudes toward creation.  Unless you decide to offer to buy it off of me after you've fired me, later.  Then, we can negotiate what I think it's worth.
I don't know anyone on the planet that would willingly work on a thing for "endless" amounts of time, catering to every whim, with no "completed" date in sight, or even standard for "what is completed".
6.  You uh... need a budget.  As already mentioned in this thread.  With a "I don't know what I actually want, and may change my mind later" type of post, it's probably best if you post what you're willing to spend on the thing.
With a budget, any prospective contractor will tell you if what you're asking for is "doable".
For perspective, I generally don't start diving into "You owe me some money for this" until I'm actually writing your story for you, instead of just consulting on it, or offering bare minimum help/editing on it.  I don't imagine other Creatives operate any differently.
Advice is free.  Short beginner lessons are free.  Anything that can be knocked out in 10 minutes... usually free.
When you start talking "months" of work (and this does sound like months of work), then you have to fork over cash.  So, how long a particular person is willing to work for you, will depend on what budget you've got to work with.
Is it $200 total?  $500?
I'd write you a 30 page (single spaced, arial font, 12 point) story for $200.  You'd probably get it in... a couple weeks, if you gave me enough to work with.  If you didn't, it might be a month.  For $500, I'd probably sit down and write you a 70 page story or so.  That's probably at minimum a month, even if you gave me everything I'd need to write it.
I don't imagine other Creatives price things differently than that.
Got $100 for a budget?  Okay, this is what I can give you for $100.
7.  You need to list which plugins you're using, so the coder can create bypasses/fixes or fix conflicts between what they're making and what you've got installed.
---
Anyway, that's all I got.
Ain't no way you're a writer.  Nor have been doing it for 15 years...  I'm stunned you would even claim that.  Offended, even.  Just... wow...
